# Tombstones: every deleted experiment

> **PERMANENT RECORD (Andrew, 2026-10-28): entries, their patches under experiments/removed/ and the inline TOMBSTONE markers are never deleted, rewritten or squashed; deletions of experiments are only ever ADDED here.**

> **Fence:** `tools/hooks/pre-push` runs `tools/tests/test_tombstones_preserved.py` on every pushed branch and on main. It refuses a push that removes or rewrites an index row, a section heading, a patch under `experiments/removed/` or an inline TOMBSTONE marker present at the merge-base with main, an index row without its section, patch or marker, or an index with fewer rows than `experiments/tombstones/index_count.txt` (raise that number when you add rows). Run it locally with `python3 tools/tests/test_tombstones_preserved.py`.

Every experiment define deleted from mojolearn, in one place. Each section says what the define tried, its verdict with the
NVIDIA / AMD ratios and the quality change as the guard message, `grid_controls` entry and `docs/apple-fast/EXPERIMENTS.md` rows
recorded them, the run ids, the sha where the code still exists, and a patch that restores it.

How to restore a deleted experiment:

1. `git apply experiments/removed/<DEFINE>.patch` from the repo root (use `git apply -3` when main has moved past the
   deletion; when a section says the patch conflicts, check the files out of the recoverable sha and merge by hand). When a
   section names an `_shared-<sha>.patch`, apply that first: it carries the deletion commit's hunks that name none of the
   defines it deleted.
2. Delete the define's refusal in its family module `core/experiment_guards_<family>.mojo` (or
   `core/six_lane_experiment_guards.mojo` for a guard shared across families) and move its entry from `removed` back to
   `controls` in `experiments/six_lane_integration/grid_controls/<lane>.json`.
3. Compile through the orchestrator (lanes never compile) and A/B it again: the old numbers are from the base they were
   measured on.

Patches are the reverse of the deletion commit restricted to code files (`.mojo`, `.py`, `.sh` outside `tools/`, `bench/` and
`docs/`; the guard file and the grid JSON are left out). A patch marked "all code hunks" is the whole deletion commit; the
others keep only the hunks that name the define. Patches generated 2026-10-09 against main `7f501620d`; the 24 patches of lane
owed-deletions-D1 (base `b639a2bd2`) are each the whole reversed deletion commit (code files only), and later D1 deletions in the
same file mean `git apply -3` where the section says so (apply in reverse deletion order to restore several).

Sources: the `removed` refusals in `core/experiment_guards_<family>.mojo` and `core/six_lane_experiment_guards.mojo`
(shared guards; split 2026-11-04, entries moved verbatim), the `removed` lists in
`experiments/six_lane_integration/grid_controls/*.json`, and the DROPPED / DELETED rows of `docs/apple-fast/EXPERIMENTS.md`.
Renamed or merged defines (code kept under a new name), promoted defines and DROP rows whose code is still on main are listed
in the tables after the sections.

## Retired by lane debt-block-per-n (2026-10-21)

These are rollback or gate arms, not measured losers: each selected a launch that the `block-per-n` / `one-block-n`
rules of `tools/hooks/no_host_routes.py` refuse (one block per output walking all n rows). The row-tile-then-fold order
that replaced them is the shape of `glm/impl/qn/glm_base.mojo::qn_tile_sum_classes`, with the host column in the same
order. No A/B was run (lanes never measure); the speed check on NVIDIA and AMD is owed with the next freeze. Code
recoverable at `28b8ed11b` (main before the lane).

### MOJOLEARN_IDN_XTY_TILED_OFF

- Tried: `core/xtdz_coalesced.mojo` `xty_launch` / `column_mean_launch` in the STATS_TPB-chain order (`xty_kernel`,
  `column_mean_kernel`: one block per column; Apple's row-coalesced `mean_partial_kernel` / `mean_fold_kernel` and
  `xtdz_coalesced` of the same chains). Also the direct `column_mean_kernel` arm of
  `decomposition/estimator.mojo::_column_variance` (`MOJOLEARN_IDN_DECOMP_MEAN_LAUNCH_OFF`), Apple FAST's
  `PCA_FAST_COLMEAN` (rab20-pcacolmean: pca taxi 106.2 -> 85.0 ms vs the one-block kernel) and `TSVD_FAST_COLVAR`
  (rab15-tsvdcolvar: tsvd taxi 40.9 -> 27.8 ms vs the one-block kernel), and `glm/impl/ridge_multi.mojo`'s Y means.
- Now: the tile order (`xty_tiled`) in every mode; host column `core/host_tile_fold.mojo` (IDN_XTY_TILED is True).
- Bits: IDENTICAL defaults unchanged; FAST and the retired arms move to the tile order.
- Files: core/xtdz_coalesced.mojo, core/host_tile_fold.mojo, decomposition/estimator.mojo, decomposition/mean_switch.mojo,
  glm/impl/ridge_multi.mojo. Patch: `experiments/removed/MOJOLEARN_IDN_XTY_TILED_OFF.patch` (reverse of lane commit
  584cd1b8c on the code files).

### MOJOLEARN_QN_TILED_MULTI_OFF

- Tried: `glm/impl/qn/glm_base.mojo::linear_bwd` with `xtdz_multi_kernel` / `xty_kernel` (one block per gradient cell)
  wherever the tile rule did not apply: `C > 1` gradients of at most 256 cells, gradients whose tile partials passed
  QNTM_MAX_WS, `-D MOJOLEARN_QN_TILED_MULTI_OFF`, IDENTICAL `C == 1` with QN_TILED off, and FAST off Apple.
- Now: `qntm_tiled_into` (chunked by the workspace bound, same chains and fold) for every `C > 1` gradient and for
  IDENTICAL's `C == 1` `linear_bwd`; FAST keeps its Apple forms. Host column `glm/host/qn_oracle.mojo` and the check
  mirrors move with it.
- Bits: narrow multinomial gradients (`d * c <= 256`) move to the tile order on NVIDIA, AMD, Apple and the host column
  together; the QN_TILED-off `C == 1` gradient likewise.
- Patch: `experiments/removed/MOJOLEARN_QN_TILED_MULTI_OFF.patch` (reverse of lane commit 4b8a8e8f2).

### MOJOLEARN_LOSS_SABOTAGE_REDUCE_SERIAL

- Tried: the loss gate's contract-5.4 sabotage, the batch's n_rows per-row losses folded by `ce_serial_fold_kernel` in
  ONE thread of one block (`training/checks/loss.mojo`), inert at N <= 128.
- Now: refused; the batch fold's witnesses are the gemm switches reached through the loss entry points.
- Bits: none (a gate-only arm).
- Patch: `experiments/removed/MOJOLEARN_LOSS_SABOTAGE_REDUCE_SERIAL.patch` (reverse of lane commit 8476d0774).

## Decomp

### The manifold kit's named x_decomp entries (2026-11-12)

Lane entangled-mkit made the manifold kit (was the Python-holding `MKit` of `bindings/mani_kit.mojo`) a typed RUN kit
(`bindings/mani_kit_run.mojo`) that calls the x_decomp image's table dispatch only. Every named entry it still called through
`MKit.fn(name)` + `family_call` became a table operation (`x_decomp/descriptor_mani_schema.mojo`, operations 120-150, the same
typed bodies with the same checks), so the 35 registrations (`bindings/_mojolearn_x_decomp.mojo`,

## GPU oracle multi-dimensional host walk

- What it was: `gbdt/methods/leaves_estimation/pointwise_oracle.mojo`'s host readback arm for the multi-dimensional leaf walk
  (`_write_multi_dim_value_and_first_derivatives`, `_write_blocked_second_derivatives`, `_mirror_second_der_row`, the OneVsAll
  arm of `write_second_derivatives`): the der and Hessian rows read back, the MultiClass pinned component, the Hessian mirror
  plus lambda, the float32 value chain and the regularize compare ran on the host for `descent_helpers.newton_like_walker_estimate`.
  Its `IDN_MULTI_HESS_ONE_WAIT` switch (`MOJOLEARN_IDN_GBDT_MULTI_HESS_ONE_WAIT_OFF`, lane/fam-gbdt, a schedule-only winner) waited
  once for the per-row readbacks; with no readbacks it has nothing to schedule.
- Verdict: removed, not an A/B loser: 11 owed `mojo-host-loop` sites (host loops on the GPU path, docs/plans/GPU_PATH_HOST_LOOPS.md).
  The walk runs on the device (`device_walker.device_multi_walk_estimate`, lane gbdt-host-loops-12); the oracle keeps an
  enqueue-only arm (`enqueue_multi_dim_evaluation`, `enqueue_multi_dim_hessian`). No NV/AMD ratios: no measurement owed for a
  deletion that the replacement path supersedes; quality is unchanged by construction (same statements, soft-float64).
- Deleted 2026-10-17 by `13299f759` on lane/gbdt-host-loops-12; recoverable at `13299f759^`.
- Patch: `experiments/removed/GBDT_ORACLE_MULTI_DIM_HOST_WALK.patch` (the deletion commit reversed, `pointwise_oracle.mojo` and
  `oracle_interface.mojo`; it also removes the host-interface kernels that commit added). Restoring it alone does not route a fit
  to the host walker: `_estimate_and_apply` refuses any walk no device walker takes.
- Guard: `MOJOLEARN_IDN_GBDT_MULTI_HESS_ONE_WAIT_OFF` refused in `gbdt/methods/leaves_estimation/pointwise_oracle.mojo` (`_check_removed_defines`, forced by `make_bin_optimized_oracle`), not in core: a core line rebuilds every binding.

## MOJOLEARN_AUTOGRAD_TRANSFORMER

Hand-glue deletion (lane del-transformer, 2026-10-19). `MOJOLEARN_AUTOGRAD_TRANSFORMER` (the old opt-in) and
`MOJOLEARN_AUTOGRAD_TRANSFORMER_OFF` (after the promotion) chose, at four seams of `bindings/_mojolearn_transformer.mojo`
(`_transformer_saved_backward`, `_transformer_run_session_backward`, `_transformer_session_backward_time`,
`_transformer_saved_backward_timed`), between the hand decoder-layer backward walk
(`transformer/checks/transformer_backward.mojo::llama_decoder_layer_backward_device`) and the autograd tape
(`autograd/rules_transformer.mojo::llama_decoder_layer_backward_autograd`, seven custom rules calling the same launchers).
The comptime switch lived in `autograd/rules_transformer.mojo`. The bindings now call the tape only; the timing entries'
slot 0 is always 1. `tools/transformer_tape_arm_check.py` is one arm, compared with `tools/transformer_tape_arm_digests.json`.

What stays: `llama_decoder_layer_backward_device` itself, because the tape refuses traced calls (identity cards),
materialized stages and non-default block options, and because training/neural_attention_owner.mojo,
byte_lm_layer_pool.mojo, byte_lm_offload.mojo, the stateless `transformer_backward` binding entry, byte_lm.mojo and
samba_resident.mojo (lanes del-lm / del-samba) call it directly. Every launcher the rules call stays.

## LLAMA_DECODER_LAYER_BACKWARD_HAND_WALK

Hand-glue deletion (lane ag-transformer-owners, 2026-10-19). No define: the walk was a function, not a switch.

- What it was: `transformer/checks/transformer_backward.mojo::llama_decoder_layer_backward_device`, the hand-written
  backward of one Llama decoder layer (stages 0-36 in launch order, an identity-card `_rec` after each), and its host-list
  wrapper `llama_decoder_layer_backward`. `MOJOLEARN_AUTOGRAD_TRANSFORMER(_OFF)` (section above) had already moved the
  bindings' session and saved-tape backwards to the tape; the walk stayed for what the tape refused (traced calls,
  materialized stages, non-default block options) and for its direct callers.
- What replaced it, per caller (all on `autograd/rules_transformer.mojo::llama_decoder_layer_backward_autograd`):
  - Traced identity cards (`transformer/checks/transformer_backward_check.mojo`, `training/checks/train_loop.mojo`,
    `transformer/checks/metal_reuse_validation.mojo`): the tape accepts the trace. `TransformerRules` holds the caller's
    `IdentityTrace` by address, the prefix and `materialize`; each rule records the walk's cards after its own launches in
    card order (Args slot i9 names a linear or rope node's cards; the gate member records 7-9 because the tape runs up
    before gate; the attention rule passes the trace into `bwd_attention_dispatch`, which records 17-21). A traced or
    materialized call keeps the entry copy into `in_d_residual2` (cards 0-1) and refuses a non-finite `d_out` before any
    card with the walk's words (`bwd_refuse_nonfinite_d_out`). The host-list `llama_decoder_layer_backward` now lives in
    `autograd/rules_transformer.mojo` on the tape. `transformer_backward_check` still compares the device cards with the
    host oracle word for word.
  - Materialized stages: `materialize` passes through to the attention dispatch, as the walk passed it.
  - Non-default block options: refused by name in the tape entry. The walk never read `w.opts`: it computed the default
    block's gradient whatever the options said, so no correct product path used it. Every remaining caller builds default
    blocks (neural_attention_owner refuses others itself; byte_lm_layer_pool / offload use `_block_weights`'s default
    record; samba_resident's session builds default blocks).
  - `training/neural_attention_owner.mojo` (both backward sites), `training/byte_lm_layer_pool.mojo`,
    `training/byte_lm_offload.mojo`, `training/checks/byte_lm_layer_pool_check.mojo`: same arguments, the tape entry.
  - The stateless `transformer_backward` binding entry (`bindings/_mojolearn_transformer.mojo::_transformer_backward_run`):
    the host-list wrapper, now on the tape.
  - `training/samba_resident.mojo`: the non-default-options fallback sat in `_backward_blocks`, an uncalled body the
    del-samba merge kept (its imports were already gone); deleted with the walk.
- Also deleted: `MOJOLEARN_AFN_LM_BWD_EPILOGUE` (and the `MOJOLEARN_AFN26_LM_BWD_EPILOGUE` alias), an Apple FAST arm
  (MERGED-UNMEASURED, lane/apple-fast-neural @ 600237d7c, no A/B ever run) that fused the gate/up and q/k/v dA fan-ins into
  one GEMM store inside the walk (`_AFN_BWD_EPI`, `_afn_route_a_resid_ok`, `_afn_bwd_epi_on`, `_afn_route_a_resid`). The
  tape never carried it, so with the walk gone nothing reads the define. `MOJOLEARN_AFN_LMGRAD_ALL` still compiles (it now
  turns the arm on with no reader). Also gone: the walk's `StepPhaseClock` / `timing_tick` diagnostics (`grad.*`,
  `bwd.*` phase names under `MOJOLEARN_STEP_PHASE_TIMERS` / `MOJOLEARN_TRANSFORMER_TIMING`).
- Verdict: DELETED (Andrew 2026-10-19: every trainer runs its backward on the tape; delete the hand glue). No new timing:
  the product path was PROMOTED under `MOJOLEARN_AUTOGRAD_TRANSFORMER` (NV + AMD average 1.01, same bits); the traced and
  materialized callers are checks, never timed. Bits: unchanged on untraced calls (same launches). Traced and materialized
  calls run the walk's launches on the walk's buffers with one difference, the entry copy is the tape's `OP_COPY` (a bit
  copy, as `bwd_copy_kernel` is). The orchestrator's check run (transformer_backward_check against the host oracle, the
  identity cards, metal_reuse_validation, train_loop, byte_lm_layer_pool_check) is owed.
- Deleted by 7b6862e3d, recoverable at 7b6862e3d^. Patch: `experiments/removed/LLAMA_DECODER_LAYER_BACKWARD_HAND_WALK.patch` (the
  deletion and its sha fill-in reversed over `transformer/checks/transformer_backward.mojo`, `autograd/rules_transformer.mojo`,
  `autograd/rules_lm.mojo`, `training/samba_resident.mojo`; it restores the walk with no callers, the callers stay on the
  tape). No grid_controls entry existed.
- Guard: `MOJOLEARN_AFN_LM_BWD_EPILOGUE` and `MOJOLEARN_AFN26_LM_BWD_EPILOGUE` refused by a `comptime assert` in
  `llama_decoder_layer_backward_autograd` (autograd/rules_transformer.mojo), not in core/six_lane_experiment_guards.mojo (the
  rebuild fence, as for `MOJOLEARN_AUTOGRAD_TRANSFORMER`). The walk had no define to refuse.
- EXPERIMENTS.md (Hand-path deletions (2026-10-19)): both rows, **DELETED (removed)**.

## MOJOLEARN_AUTOGRAD_CNN_OFF

- What it was: the hand-chained CNNClassifier backward in `bindings/_mojolearn_x_cnn.mojo` `fit_epoch_r_binding` and
  `fit_epoch_d_binding`: per step `linear_backward_into[True]` for the head into the last block's gout, then
  `conv_block_backward_into[True]` per block from last to first, chaining each block's input gradient by hand. The
  `AUTOGRAD_CNN` switch in `autograd/rules_cnn.mojo` (default on; `MOJOLEARN_AUTOGRAD_CNN_OFF` selected the hand walk,
  `MOJOLEARN_AUTOGRAD_CNN` the opt-in spelling) picked it against `cnn_backward_autograd`. The fused kernels stay: the tape
  rules (`CNN_CONV_BLOCK`, `CNN_LINEAR`) call them with the same arguments in the same order.
- Files: `bindings/_mojolearn_x_cnn.mojo`, `autograd/rules_cnn.mojo`, `x_cnn/checks/tape_check.mojo` (its hand arm and the
  tape-vs-hand compare).
- Verdict: removed (Andrew 2026-10-19: every trainer runs its backward on the tape by default; delete the hand glue). Not an
  A/B loser: the default was flipped on the word-for-word check without timing, and no hand-vs-tape timing run exists for the
  CNN trainer (TM_LM_TIMING, NV_PASS5, AMD_PASS5 and the pass-6 reports have no CNN row), so there are no NV/AMD ratios.
  Quality unchanged by construction: same bits.
- Evidence: `x_cnn/checks/tape_check.mojo`, tape vs hand, 96 rows (per case 3 losses and 21 tensor digests; cases
  sgd/adam x pool+saved / nopool+recompute) all SAME on integration fda883af2: Metal compile-22 (`cnn-tape-run.log`), NVIDIA L40S
  and AMD MI325X p6-01 (`checks/cnn-tape-run.log`) and final-02 (`cnn-run.log`), all five printing the same 96 rows
  (~/mojolearn-evidence/autograd-buildout-20261019/). Those rows are now stored in `x_cnn/checks/tape_check_digests.tsv`
  and the check compares the tape against them (e.g. sgd.pool.saved loss step 0 2.3037658, block0.w grad 8104314183148238768).
- Deleted 2026-10-19 by `ddd4fa509` on lane/del-cnn; recoverable at `ddd4fa509^`.
- Patch: `experiments/removed/MOJOLEARN_AUTOGRAD_CNN_OFF.patch` (the three code files, from the lane head back to
  `ddd4fa509^`; it also removes the inline tombstones and the refusals).
- Guard: `MOJOLEARN_AUTOGRAD_CNN_OFF` and the opt-in spelling `MOJOLEARN_AUTOGRAD_CNN` refused in `autograd/rules_cnn.mojo`
  (`cnn_backward_autograd`, reached by every CNN trainer step), not in core: a core line rebuilds every binding (the
  pre-push rebuild fence refuses it). No `grid_controls` entry existed.

## Framework adapter per-operation surfaces

- What it was: one mojolearn operation per framework call. PyTorch: `torch.ops.mojolearn.operation(inputs, code,
  output_shape, options, scalars, integer_output, device)` (`adapters/torch/registration.cpp` `operation` and
  `operation_meta`). MAX: the custom ops `mojolearn_matmul`, `mojolearn_relu` and `mojolearn_operation0..3`
  (`adapters/max_ops/__init__.mojo`, `execute_operation`). Native: the C entries `mojolearn_adapter_operation` and
  `mojolearn_adapter_operation_host_buffers` (`adapters/native/c_api.mojo`, `adapters/native/abi.h`) over
  `run_operation` (`adapters/native/operation.mojo`, an `OpsSession` per call). Their checkers went with them:
  `tools/check_max_native_adapters.py`, `tools/check_native_adapter_abi.py`, `tools/check_native_adapter_transport.py`,
  `tools/check_max_adapter_fault.py`, the per-op fault controls of `tools/check_native_adapter_faults.py` (wrong-operation,
  stall), `adapters/direct_equivalence_check.mojo`, and the unconnected per-op payload draft `tools/adapter_payload.py`
  (+ `tools/test_adapter_payload.py`). The per-op checks in `tools/check_native_adapters.py` became the whole-model
  torch-compile phase.
- Verdict: removed as API, not an experiment (Andrew, 2026-10-24): mojolearn integrates with PyTorch and MAX only as
  whole-model programs. Between per-op calls the framework computes with its own bits, which breaks the cross-vendor
  identity contract, and we do not want part of mojolearn used inside a framework graph. No timing or quality numbers:
  nothing was measured against it. The per-op names were already undocumented (`docs-site/api_exclude.txt`); those rows
  are deleted with the code.
- What remains public: `torch.compile(model, backend="mojolearn")`, `mojolearn.import_model(module)`,
  `torch.ops.mojolearn.train`, the MAX `mojolearn_train` / `mojolearn_train_resume` ops, and the native
  `mojolearn_adapter_abi` / `mojolearn_adapter_train` entries they call. The training path never used the per-op
  entries; `adapters/native/operation.mojo` keeps only the descriptor helpers training shares.
- Last sha with them: `b022e2ea5` (main). Deleted on lane/adapters-whole-model-20261024 by `761a927d6` and the commits
  after it; recoverable at `761a927d6^` (= `b022e2ea5`). No patch: removed API, not an experiment define.
- Guard: `tools/test_adapter_surfaces.py` fails if the registration, the MAX package, the native exports or `abi.h` name
  anything but the whole-model entries; `packaging/adapters/build.sh` refuses a native library exporting
  `mojolearn_adapter_operation*`; `tools/check_native_adapters.py` fails if `torch.ops.mojolearn.operation` resolves.
  They must not come back (AGENTS.md "Framework adapters are the same API in another format").

## Implicit Python model capture (2026-10-27)

Owner-authorized API change during provider migration: `import_model` accepts an
exported ONNX path or native reader graph. Implicit `torch.nn.Module` export,
`ModelProto.SerializeToString`, the `example_inputs` argument, automatic
TorchDynamo backend registration and automatic changed-weight re-export are
removed. Direct imports of the former backend receive a native refusal.
`ImportedProgram.run_torch` uses the existing whole-model native executor.
Graph/weights are imported explicitly; input metadata is captured per execution.
The implementation is on the provider integration branch pending compilation and
public runtime qualification; this entry is not release or performance evidence.

## MOJOLEARN_IDN_MAMBA1_CHUNKED_SCAN

- **What it tried** (lane mamba-folds, 2026-10-28; idea 11 of the 2026-10-28 neural report, roadmap B5): the Mamba-1
  selective scan as a chunked parallel scan. Chunks of W = 64 tokens were anchored at the first token of each CALL. Inside a
  chunk the affine map `(P, Lc)` folded serially (`P = da`, `Lc = dbu`, then `P = ftz(da * P)`,
  `Lc = ftz(fma(da, Lc, dbu))`) and the state was `ftz(fma(P, H_k, Lc))`. The chunk-entry states `H_k` were carried serially.
  It ran as three cell launches (summaries, carry, outputs) plus a backward-checkpoint variant. The host column and both host
  oracles carried the same fold.
- **Files**: `mamba/impl/ops/m1_chunked_scan.mojo` (new, and its generated twin `mamba/host/gen/m1_chunked_scan.mojo`).
  Wiring in `mamba/impl/ops/selective_scan_interface.mojo` (selective_scan_fn) and
  `autograd/kernels/mamba1_scan.mojo` (selective_scan_checkpoint_fn). Oracle fold `M1ChainFold` in
  `mamba/checks/mamba_oracle.mojo`, used by `mamba/checks/mamba_backward_oracle.mojo`. `tools/mamba_host_gen.py` SOURCES entry.
  Contract note in `mamba/IDENTICAL_MAMBA_CONTRACT.md` section 10.
- **Verdict**: REJECTED: breaks decode==prefill at 64-token chunk boundaries (owner decision 2026-10-28, relayed by the
  orchestrator). A one-token decode call kept the v1 bits, but a multi-token prefill re-associated at every chunk boundary.
  A generation's bits would therefore depend on how its tokens were fed: a semantics change, not a fold-order change.
  No A/B was run and no NVIDIA/AMD ratio exists (not measured). Quality: not measured.
- **Run ids**: none. It compiled green on the CPU column and sm_89 at lane/mamba-folds@139c65a5dc
  (experiments/mamba_folds_20261028/compile.json at that commit).
- **Recoverable**: lane/mamba-folds@db803a1337 (the code never reached main, so there is no patch file).
- **Guard**: `mamba/impl/ops/selective_scan_interface.mojo::selective_scan_fn` refuses `-D MOJOLEARN_IDN_MAMBA1_CHUNKED_SCAN` (in the area's own module: the pre-push rebuild fence refuses edits to `core/six_lane_experiment_guards.mojo`). The removed entry is in
  `experiments/six_lane_integration/grid_controls/mamba-folds.json`; the `docs/apple-fast/EXPERIMENTS.md` row says REJECTED.
- **For a future chunking lane**: anchor the chunks at ABSOLUTE token positions, not at the start of each call. Carry the open
  chunk's state across decode calls (the chunk-entry state, the running `(P, Lc)` and the position within the chunk), as the
  Mamba-2 decode carries its open chunk (DEVIATION 786). Then a decode step and a prefill fold every token identically, and
  decode == prefill holds by construction. That changes the decode state the bindings carry, so it is a state-ABI change.

## Executor loop driver loops (2026-11-08)

- **What it was**: three hand-written loop drivers replaced by the executor's bounded loop
  (`autograd/program_loop.mojo`, `autograd/program_loop_device.mojo`; docs/plans/AUTOGRAD_API.md "Bounded loops").
  (1) The IDENTICAL k-means Lloyd chunk loop in `cluster/impl/detail/kmeans.mojo::kmeans_fit_main_traced`
  (`IDN_KMEANS_DEVICE_CONV`: gated assignment, gated row-block accumulations, finalize, shift, gated copy back and the
  device criterion, enqueued KMEANS_CONV_CHUNK iterations per flag read). It is now the step op `LloydStep` run by
  `bounded_device_loop`: the same kernels, arguments and order, so no bit moves. (2) `kmeans_conv_step_kernel`
  (`cluster/checks/reduce_by_key.mojo`), merged into the generic criterion op `loop_below_kernel`, which also stores the
  iteration register (a word no k-means output reads). (3) `_copy_state` in `autograd/program_control.mojo`: the
  program `while_loop` copied every carried state tensor into a fresh buffer and drained the executor per iteration,
  after a host read of the condition (two drains per iteration). The loop now carries the state in place
  (OP_LOOP_COMMIT, a gated bit copy), tests the condition on the device (OP_LOOP_TICK) and reads the register block
  every `check_every` iterations (one drain per iteration at the default 1). Same outputs, `iterations` and `stopped`.
- **Versions and measurements**: the k-means loop had two IDENTICAL forms, the device-criterion chunk loop (default since
  fam2-cluster, 0372975724, 2026-10-04) and the per-iteration drain (`-D MOJOLEARN_IDN_KMEANS_DEVICE_CONV_OFF`). No
  standalone A/B of the two exists; the chunk loop is the form behind every recorded kmeans cell (paper 0.8.55
  istella fit 405.7 ms, taxi 191.6 ms on MI300X) and the chunk size 8 kept by A08 (chunk 1: AMD 0.83-0.99x, NVIDIA mixed;
  `cluster/impl/detail/kmeans.mojo` KMEANS_CONV_CHUNK note). Kept: the chunk loop's order, now on the executor. The
  per-iteration drain stays as the `_OFF` B arm and as the form for `inertia_check`, the identity trace, multi-device
  assignment and FAST. A/B owed: DEVICE_CONV on vs off on NVIDIA and AMD (kmeans istella, taxi, one non-board shape).
  The program `while_loop` had one form; no measurement exists; bits are unchanged by construction.
- **Verdict**: REFACTORED (no define removed, no bit change). Quality: unchanged (same words).
- **Run ids**: none (lanes never run; RUN OWED in the lane reply).
- **Recoverable**: `22ac89b54c` (origin/main at the lane's base); deleted on lane/fix-d3-executor-loops.
- **Patch**: `experiments/removed/EXECUTOR_LOOP_DRIVER_LOOPS.patch`, `git diff <lane head> 22ac89b54c --
  cluster/impl/detail/kmeans.mojo cluster/checks/reduce_by_key.mojo autograd/program_control.mojo`; `git apply`
  restores the three files on the lane head, `git apply -3` once main has moved.
- **Guard / records**: no `-D` define was removed, so no guard refusal and no `grid_controls` entry moves. One row in
  `docs/apple-fast/EXPERIMENTS.md`.

  (`_arena_io.DeviceRows`) reached a host-address kernel as a device gather out of the resident base, a DOWNLOAD of
  the rows, a host finiteness scan of them and the kernel's re-upload. `admit_x` (`bindings/admitted_input.mojo`
  `_admitted_rows`) now reads the fold itself: with `device_x=True` it returns the handle (base, indices) with no host
  words, for an entry that gathers on the device; otherwise it gathers the rows on the host straight out of the host

  is the array-returning form for a door that still hands its owners an array.

  reach the kernel. Refusals keep their wording; an out-of-range index is now refused at the door (`IndexError`).

## RFE one program per elimination round (2026-11-09)

Lane `w1-readmission-rfe` (plan `docs/plans/EXECUTOR_CONSOLIDATION_AND_CLEANUP.md` section 4, row RFE), branch
`lane/w1-readmission-rfe` from `origin/integ/pre-0867` `f7d10d2b09`; deletion commit `d6f2d5ed09`. Not an experiment
define: a re-admission defect. `bindings/prep_select_native.mojo` ran two x_prep programs per elimination round (a
gather program `_gather_cls` putting X and gathering the active columns, then the importance keys + `c2_rfe_step` +
`c2_rfe_rank`), one more gather program for the final fit, rebuilt the active-column list and the support mask on the
host every round, and fell back silently to putting X every round when the resident scope could not be entered.

Now one program per round: the importance keys, `c2_rfe_step`, `c2_rfe_rank`, then `_stage_block` (the new x_prep op
`c2_rfe_keep` 271, the supported columns compacted on the device, and `gather_cols` from the resident X) stages the next
round's block in the same program; program 0 stages the first block. The resident scope is required (entering it only
records the scope; the rows owner connects when the package imports `model_selection`). The support is read on the host
once, after the last round. Programs per fit: 2R + 1 -> R + 1. No bit change: the same stages on the same words, and the
gather is bit for bit. Deleted: `_gather_cls`, the per-round host `features` / `mask` lists, the no-scope fallback.

Restore: `git apply -3 experiments/removed/W1_RFE_GATHER_PROGRAM_PER_ROUND.patch` (the reverse of `d6f2d5ed09` on
`bindings/prep_select_native.mojo`; op 271 may stay). Run owed: RFE speed on NVIDIA and AMD (paper_compare / board RFE
rows) against `f7d10d2b09`, and the RFE identity lane at the release.

Same lane. The public `randomized_svd` (`bindings/linalg_decomp_native.mojo`) sequenced `_rsvd_core` and `_flip_u`
through the binding decomp kit: one py_call into an x_decomp entry per step (about 40 for n_iter 4), with `_flip_u`
moving U and Vt to the process-default mode's kit when the selected mode differed. It is now ONE call,
`x_decomp_randomized_svd` (`x_decomp/randomized_svd_owner.mojo`, door `providers/python/x_decomp_rsvd_owner_pyapi.mojo`,
device and host bindings): `pca_randomized_core` on `RKit` (the kit PCA and TruncatedSVD randomized already run on) with
the orientation given, then `svd_flip(u_based_decision=True)` in the selected mode. The switches below only chose how
the old sequence moved M; the driver always reads M in place and uploads it once, so no route is left to select.

- `MOJOLEARN_RSVD_FAST_DIRECT_IN` (FAST + Apple default, M3 `e9d72edb5`: istella 517.3 -> 501.3 ms) and
  `MOJOLEARN_IDN_RSVD_DIRECT_IN` (IDENTICAL default, grid `g50ebe26a5`: the `_OFF` arm 1.931x slower combined): M from the
  caller's buffer straight into a pooled device matrix. Deleted with their `x_decomp_w4_flags` entry (no other bit was
  left), its door `w4_flags_py` and the uncalled Python `w4_flags` reader; `x_decomp/w4_fast.mojo` and
  `providers/python/x_decomp_w4_fast_pyapi.mojo` keep their tombstones only. `grid_controls/fg-pca.json`
  `rsvd_idn_direct_in` moved to `removed`.
- `MOJOLEARN_RSVD_FAST_DEVSCAN` (FAST + Apple default, rab15: istella 490.1 -> 435.1 ms with ORTH_WS): the finiteness
  refusal on the device copy instead of the serial host scan. The serial scan it beat is gone (the one admission path's
  parallel host scan); deleted with `dev_upload_scan_run`, `dev_upload_scan_py`, `x_decomp_dev_upload_scan` and bit 1 of
  `x_decomp_s_flags`.
- Also deleted: `DecompKit.orth`, `order_small`, `grown` and `_same_mode` (only the old sequence used them).
- Refusal of the `_OFF` names in `core/experiment_guards_decomposition.mojo`. Bits: randomized_svd's may change (the sign
  flip now runs in the selected mode's binding; every step follows RKit's residency), the same on NVIDIA, AMD and Apple
  within the version. RUN OWED: the randomized-svd row on NVIDIA and AMD (speed), the randomized_svd identity lane.
- Code recoverable at `f7d10d2b09`; patch `experiments/removed/A3_ADMISSION_HELPERS.patch`.
- **Restored 2026-11-09** (lane r1-restore-measured-winners; AGENTS.md "A measured winner is never deleted on reasoning"): `MOJOLEARN_RSVD_FAST_DEVSCAN` restored 2026-11-09 by fe8ea8a804 as behaviour inside the one call: the one driver did NOT do the same work (its admission scans M on the host, in parallel: a host pass the measured default never paid). The caller defers M's finite test when `x_decomp_s_flags` bit 1 is set (FAST + Apple) and the driver tests the device copy at M's one upload (RKit.device_tested -> RDev.upload_finite -> resident.mojo dev_upload_finite_run); `-D MOJOLEARN_RSVD_FAST_DEVSCAN_OFF` is the A/B arm again. `MOJOLEARN_RSVD_FAST_DIRECT_IN` / `MOJOLEARN_IDN_RSVD_DIRECT_IN` stay deleted, proven by the code: the one driver borrows a C float32 M (no host copy) and uploads it once into a pooled device matrix from the caller's buffer (RKit.device: Self.D.alloc = pool_alloc, D.upload = dev_upload_run), the work both switches did. No bit change. Owed row `r1-rsvd-devscan` (Apple FAST, paused).

## Executor gated state and chunked loop (2026-11-08)

- **What it was**: two loop mechanisms that the executor's gate now makes unnecessary (lane
  x1b-executor-gated-state-chunked-loop; docs/plans/EXECUTOR_X1_API.md section 5). (1) In
  `autograd/program_control.mojo control_prepare`, a `while_loop` body holding a block step op (`is_block_step`) with
  a condition was forced to `check_every = 1`: one status read per iteration, because the step op writes the
  session's state in place, not behind the gate. Every solver loop moved onto the executor with in-place state was
  therefore no better than its hand loop (which polls every 8-16 iterations). Now every declared state parameter of
  the body is shadowed behind the gate (`OP_LOOP_SHADOW` after each body: open, the shadow takes the value; closed,
  the live tensor gets the committed value back), resident step entries are rebuilt after bodies past the stop, a
  blind body's error past the stop is dropped, and the loop reads once per chunk for every body; `check_every` /
  `unroll` default to the chunk rule (`loop_auto_chunk`). (2) `autograd/program_runtime.mojo
  train_program_control`'s epoch loop: an ungated host loop with no stopping criterion (the loss curve an ungated
  copy, no iteration register). It is now the bounded device loop: `OP_LOOP_OPEN` per epoch, a gated loss commit,
  `OP_LOOP_FIT_TICK` (the device iteration register and scikit-learn SGD's `tol` / `n_iter_no_change` rule), one
  read per `fit_epochs_per_read` epochs, parameters and optimizer moments shadowed and the host optimizer scalars
  restored for epochs past the stop. Returns the epochs run.
- **Versions and measurements**: one form each; no measurement exists. Kept: the gated forms. The per-iteration
  read stays reachable as `check_every=1` (and is what the chunk rule picks for a body whose in-place state is
  above `LOOP_DRAIN_FLOATS`). A/B owed: a Mamba-1 / Mamba-3 decode `while_loop` with an EOS condition, default
  vs `check_every=1`, and Program.fit with and without `tol` (SGD shapes of lane N3b), on NVIDIA and AMD.
- **Verdict**: REFACTORED (no define removed). Bits: none for any existing program (the shadows and gates are bit
  copies; the fit's curve copy is now a gated bit copy of the same value; the optimizer steps are unchanged).
  Quality: unchanged.
- **Run ids**: none (lanes never run; RUN OWED in the lane reply).
- **Recoverable**: `f59d913b0b` (origin/integ/pre-0867-w2 at the lane's base; the forced read never reached main,
  the fit loop did); deleted on lane/x1b-executor-gated-state-chunked-loop.
- **Patch**: `experiments/removed/EXECUTOR_GATED_STATE_CHUNKED_LOOP.patch`, `git diff <lane head> f59d913b0b --`
  the lane's code files (autograd/program_control.mojo, program_runtime.mojo, program_entries.mojo,
  program_loop.mojo, the three providers/python doors, python/mojolearn/ops.py, the two experiments compile
  wrappers); `git apply` restores them on the lane head, `git apply -3` once main has moved.
- **Guard / records**: no `-D` define was removed, so no guard refusal and no `grid_controls` entry moves. One row in
  `docs/apple-fast/EXPERIMENTS.md`.
## Labels and trees admission copy onto the one path (2026-11-09)

Lane `a1b-doors-opt-in-trees-linear` (A1b of `docs/plans/EXECUTOR_CONSOLIDATION_AND_CLEANUP.md` section 3.3, finishing
A1 on A5's `admit_x` options), branch `lane/a1b-doors-opt-in-trees-linear` from `integ/pre-0867-w2` `f59d913b0b`. Not
experiment defines: the second admission path in `bindings/classical_labels.mojo` (and its `trees_*` aliases in
`bindings/trees_public_inputs.mojo`), a cast-and-view copy beside `bindings/admitted_input.mojo` with its own view
struct, no finite test of X and zero-filled destinations. No A/B: the same words reach every kernel (one conversion
per element in both paths; a borrowed float32 C-order input is borrowed in both).

- `labels_f32` / `trees_f32` / `labels_f32_view` / `labels_forest_layout`: `admit_x_unrecorded` for a public X,
  `admit_f32` (the array form as an `AdmittedX`, `ndim` -1 any rank up to 2) for targets, fitted arrays and published
  predictions, `order="F"` for the F-order layouts. Where the old path tested nothing, `allow_nonfinite=True` keeps that.
- `LabelsMatrix` / `TreesMatrix`: `AdmittedX` (now `Copyable`); the constructor is `admitted_words`.
- `labels_empty` / `labels_vector` / `trees_empty` / `trees_vector`: `admitted_array` / `admitted_vector`, the one
  zero-filled Array allocator (`admitted_storage(..., as_array=True)` is the same call).
- `labels_view` / `LabelsView` / `trees_view` / `TreesView` / `_view_of_array` / `_view_of_buffer` /
  `labels_check_rank` / `labels_shape_repr`: `admit_c_view` (any numeric dtype in C order: the exporter's view, or one
  C-order copy of a strided export) with `admitted_dtype`; integer vectors through `admit_ids` (one parallel read of the
  exporter's strides, `core/admitted_ids.mojo`). The label encoder reads its block through `admit_c_view`
  (`classical_encode_words` is the encoder over a contiguous block); an F-ordered label matrix is now its C-order copy
  (the same values in the same order as the label input step, so the same classes and codes).
- `labels_check_sample_weight` / `labels_prepare_weights` / `trees_*`: `admit_weight_words` (`admit_weights`; None is
  the ones vector).
- `labels_all_finite` / `trees_all_finite`: `core/host_finite_scan.mojo` directly where a label vector is tested.
- `trees_encode_labels`: the trees copy of the encoder is gone; it returns `classical_encode_labels`' classes and codes.
  Behaviour: str-subclass labels, which the trees copy refused, are encoded like str (the shared encoder's rule).
- Trees internals (`trees_public_boost` `_gather_view` / `_gather_codes_view` / `_gather_vec_view`, `trees_public_meta`
  `_place_view`, `trees_explainer_native` `_snapshot`'s serial strided copy, `trees_public_iforest` `_copied`): the
  helpers take the Arrays themselves; meta Y and explainer snapshots are read in C order (one C-order copy of an
  F-ordered or strided input; same values).
- `decomp_input_snapshot` (PLS's own cast and scan): `_pls_input` in `bindings/pls_native.mojo`.
- `core/admitted_transpose.mojo`: no caller left.
- The prep_labels multilabel F-order arm (base `transpose_f32`) and the KNeighborsClassifier column-major y branch: y is
  read in C order.

Also in the lane (not removals): the x_linear decision entries (`x_linear_decision` / `_codes` / `_rows`, GPU and host
column) take an optional status-word address as their last dims element and test the X they upload
(`core/admitted_finite_status.mojo`); x_linear fit and predict doors and the forest / IsolationForest fit doors pass
`defer_finite=True` (their entries test the upload); the array form of `admit_x` consults the meta-estimator registry.

Restore: `git apply -3 experiments/removed/A1B_LABELS_ADMISSION_COPY.patch` (the reverse of the lane's code changes
from `f59d913b0b`). Run owed: the linear (sgd, ridge, huber, glm, enet, lasso, logistic), trees (rf, extratrees,
iforest, gbdt, meta) and prep / neighbors rows of the board on NVIDIA and AMD, and the release's one identity record.

## N9: every dense eigh on the executor ops (2026-11-09)

Lane n9-decomp-eigh-families (branch lane/n9-decomp-eigh-families, base origin/integ/pre-0867-w2 f59d913b0b;
docs/plans/EXECUTOR_CONSOLIDATION_AND_CLEANUP.md section 4, docs/plans/EXECUTOR_N7_OPS.md).

  (x_decomp/eigh_ops.mojo): `eigh_op_sym` (new: `DevExec.eigh`'s own route, the tridiagonal solve from TD_MIN_N on a
  copy with the Jacobi of the input enqueued behind it and chosen on the device on a refusal, the one-block Jacobi
  below) and `eigh_op_dense` (batched one-block Jacobi). `eigh_td_on` became `eigh_td_enqueue` (no refusal drain).
  The host column runs `eigh_op_sym_host` / `eigh_op_dense_host` (`HostExec.eigh_batch` is now parallel over the
  problems). Resident kits keep w and V on the device: `DKit.eigh` (FastICA symmetric decorrelation, FactorAnalysis EM,
  the rotation, MinCovDet's pinvh with its cut taken on the device), `IpcaDev.eigh_desc` / `DecompDev.eigh_desc`

  Lanczos T solve is `eigh_op_tridiag` on the device alphas / betas (`x_decomp_dev_eigh_tridiag`), the host column
  `eigh_op_tridiag_host` (`x_decomp_eigh_tridiag`). The spectral Lanczos projected solve keeps the Jacobi at every ncv
  (`DevExec._eigh_jacobi_on` on `eigh_op_dense`), as its host oracle.

  `xd_first_where2_enq` / `xd_first_where2_kernel`, x_decomp/rr_block_device.mojo (the device arm of the quarantined

  host-word route, the Lanczos host T assembly in `x_decomp/kpca_owner.mojo` and `bindings/mani_decomp_native.mojo`.

## GP, GPC and KRR on the executor's Cholesky ops (2026-11-09)

Lane n8-gp-krr-smo (docs/plans/EXECUTOR_CONSOLIDATION_AND_CLEANUP.md section 4, rows "GP regressor / GPC Laplace"
and "KRR"; the ops are lane N7's, docs/plans/EXECUTOR_N7_OPS.md). Every Gaussian process and kernel ridge Cholesky now
runs `chol_op_factor` / `chol_op_cho_solve` / `chol_op_logdet` (cholesky/chol_ops.mojo): the factor's `info` stays in a
device word that gates the later launches (CHOL_DEFER_INFO on every vendor) and comes home at the family's own sync.

- `MOJOLEARN_IDN_GPC_NEWTON_LOGDET_OFF` (the `_OFF` arm of GPC_IDN_NEWTON_LOGDET, fam2-kernel-gp 2026-10-04, IDENTICAL
  default ON, no A/B of its own: the default kept log|B| on the device, the arm read it home per iteration through
  `chol_logdet`). The Newton loop is now one bounded device loop, so the host read the arm restored has nowhere to go;
  the log-determinant is always `chol_op_logdet`. No `grid_controls` entry existed. Refusal in
  `core/experiment_guards_kernel.mojo`.
- The two copies of the Laplace Newton loop (`classifier.mojo::_gpc_fit_binary_device` and
  `gpc_ovr.mojo::gpc_newton_device`, the same launches in the same order) and the seven ungated kernels only they
  launched (`gpc_b_matrix_kernel`, `gpc_w_kernel`, `gpc_rhs_kernel`, `gpc_scale_nan_kernel`, `gpc_a_kernel`,
  `gpc_lml_part_kernel`, `gpc_lml_fin_kernel`, plus `gpc_ovr.mojo::gpc_lml_fin_dev_kernel`): replaced by
  `gaussian_process/gpc_newton.mojo` (`GPCNewtonStep` on `bounded_device_loop`, the same items gated on the loop's done
  word, the NaN guard and DEVIATION 2830's stop test as one criterion kernel). Per fit: 2-3 drains per Newton iteration
  became one register read per 8 iterations plus one read of the likelihood. The `+0.0` `add_jitter` launch on B was
  dropped: B's diagonal is `ftz(1 + cell)`, never -0.0, so it changed no bit.
- `gp_opt_run_end_kernel` and `gpr_optimize_device`'s per-run host loop (the stop word read after every evaluation,
  the Cholesky's `info` read inside `potrf_lower`): replaced by `gp_opt_advance_kernel` (`gp_opt_advance_item`: a stopped
  run's record and the next run's start on the device) and a done word read once per 8 evaluations
  (`GP_OPT_EVAL_CHECK`).
- Also moved, no record of their own: `gpr_resident.mojo::gpr_fit_ptr_device`, `estimator.mojo::gpr_fit_host`,
  `gpr_lml_grad_host` (four drains to one) and `gpr_sample_y_host`; KRR's `kernel_ridge_solve` off the trace route and
  `kernel_ridge_fit_ptr` (info read with the dual download; new `kernel_ridge_factor_solve_enqueue`).
  `chol_op_zero_on_fail` was added to cholesky/chol_ops.mojo for the failed-fit zero dual.
- Bits: none intended on NVIDIA, AMD or Apple IDENTICAL (the ops run `potrf_lower`'s strip / left-looking launches and
  `cho_solve`'s chains, and the GPC items and block sizes are unchanged). A failed factor's returned L is the one frozen
  at the failing panel rather than LAPACK's completed partial factor. Apple FAST GP / GPC / KRR words change (strip
  schedule instead of the vendor-GEMM panel route; FAST needs quality only).
- Code recoverable at `f59d913b0b`; patches `experiments/removed/N8_GPC_NEWTON_ONE_LOOP.patch` (classifier.mojo,
  gpc_ovr.mojo) and `experiments/removed/N8_GP_OPT_DEVICE_RUNS.patch` (gp_optim.mojo, gp_optim_items.mojo).

## EM driver loops onto the device loop (2026-11-09)

- **What it was**: lane n1-gmm-bgmm-loops (plan docs/plans/EXECUTOR_CONSOLIDATION_AND_CLEANUP.md section 4, rows GMM EM
  and BayesianGMM). (1) `mixture/estimator.mojo::gaussian_mixture_fit`'s host EM loop: E-step, M-step and
  `gmm_precision_cholesky` per iteration, the mean log-likelihood copied home and `abs(change) < tol` decided on the host
  (one drain per iteration, plus the pivot-flag drain of the precision Cholesky), the `MOJOLEARN_STAGE_TIMES` phase
  timers, and `IDN_GMM_ONE_DRAIN` (`-D MOJOLEARN_IDN_GMM_ONE_DRAIN_OFF`), which moved the meanll copy onto the pivot
  drain. It is now the step op `GmmEmStep` run by `bounded_device_loop` (autograd/program_loop_device.mojo): the same
  E-step, M-step and precision kernels, the pivot verdict as a device word that joins the loop (`step_fail_joins_loop`),
  a gated commit of the parameters (`gmm_em_commit_kernel`) and the criterion on the device
  (`gmm_em_criterion_kernel`: the same `gmm_convergence_change` / `gmm_converged` float32 comparison). Per-op timing is
  `-D MOJOLEARN_EXECUTOR_TIMERS` (`loop_lap`). (2) The one-launch precision factors (IDN fused, FAST fused, FAST big) and
  their host readback of the pivot flags moved from `gmm_precision_cholesky` to `gmm_precision_enqueue`
  (mixture/checks/mstep.mojo); at d above those kernels' range the per-component chain runs on the N7 Cholesky ops
  (`chol_op_factor`, `chol_op_logdet`, `chol_op_solve_lower`) instead of `potrf_lower` / `chol_logdet` / `trsm_lower`
  with their per-panel `info` and logdet reads; `gmm_precision_cholesky` keeps the sabotage arms only. (3)
  `x_cluster/bgmm.mojo::bgmm_fit`'s read of the scalar block every iteration: the loop now ends each iteration with a
  gated commit of the workspace (ST_COMMIT) and a stop word (ST_FREEZE), and reads the two-word freeze pair once per
  `check_every` iterations. The read interval is `core/em_loop_chunk.mojo` (8 below 2**24 multiply-adds an iteration,
  else 1; host column 1; trace, sabotage and row-sharded E-step 1).
- **Versions and measurements**: one form of each loop existed (plus the ONE_DRAIN `_OFF` arm: I21 2026-10-06 OFF/ON
  NVIDIA 1.010/1.020/1.532, AMD 0.987/1.000/1.010, kept ON). No A/B of the device loop exists; at the board shapes
  (gmm / bayesian-gmm istella, taxi: above the work bound) the interval is 1, one read per iteration as before.
- **Verdict**: REFACTORED. Bits: unchanged by construction for every fit whose precision Cholesky took a fused kernel
  (IDENTICAL d <= 256, FAST Apple d <= 256) and for BGMM; the committed parameters are the stopping iteration's for any
  interval. At d above the fused range the chain's words are the N7 ops' (potrf_lower's launches at the pinned width,
  the default trsm kernels, the logdet fold): expected equal, re-recorded with the gmm identity lane at the release run.
- **Recoverable**: `f59d913b0b` (origin/integ/pre-0867-w2 at the lane's base); deleted on lane/n1-gmm-bgmm-loops.
- **Patch**: `experiments/removed/EXECUTOR_EM_DRIVER_LOOPS.patch`, `git diff <lane head> f59d913b0b --
  mixture/estimator.mojo mixture/checks/mstep.mojo x_cluster/bgmm.mojo`; `git apply` restores the three files on the
  lane head (drop the `MOJOLEARN_IDN_GMM_ONE_DRAIN_OFF` refusal in core/experiment_guards_cluster.mojo to build the
  `_OFF` arm), `git apply -3` once the base has moved.
- **Guard / records**: `MOJOLEARN_IDN_GMM_ONE_DRAIN_OFF` refused in core/experiment_guards_cluster.mojo; no
  `grid_controls` entry existed. Rows in `docs/apple-fast/EXPERIMENTS.md`.

## MDS, label propagation and NMF loops on the bounded device loop (2026-11-09)

Lane `n4-mds-labelprop-nmf-loops` (plan `docs/plans/EXECUTOR_CONSOLIDATION_AND_CLEANUP.md` section 4, rows MDS SMACOF,
Label propagation, NMF multiplicative / CD), branch `lane/n4-mds-labelprop-nmf-loops` from `origin/integ/pre-0867-w2`
`f59d913b0b`. Not experiment defines except the two label-propagation rollbacks: host loops that read a word home every
iteration, moved onto the executor's bounded device loop (`autograd/program_loop_device.mojo`, the `LoopStep` KMeans'
Lloyd loop uses). Each body writes its carried state only through `DKit.put_gated` (x_decomp) or gated kernels
(x_neighbors), so iterations enqueued past the stop leave it as the stopping iteration left it, and ends with a
one-thread criterion kernel; the host reads the register block once per chunk.

- MDS SMACOF (`x_decomp/mds_dev.mojo`): Y, d and the raw stress / ssd words are the state; the stop test is
  `mds_smacof_crit_kernel` over `mds_stop_f32` and the non-metric disparity scale is a device scalar (OP_DIV, OP_SQRT
  cells). Reads per iteration 2-3 -> 1 per 8 iterations (MDS_LOOP_CHUNK) + 1 per start.
- NMF (`x_decomp/nmf_dev.mojo`): MU writes W, H through `put_gated` and tests `nmf_err_f32` / `nmf_mu_stop_f32` every 10
  iterations on the device (a zero first error stops the loop with failure code 1, the driver returns NMF_ZERO_ERR0); the
  register block is read every 10 iterations, exactly where the old loop branched. CD sweeps a copy of W / Ht
  (`DKit.cd_rows_enq`, `cd_rows_kernel` unchanged) and writes it back gated, the coordinate order stays a device value
  (identity uploaded once, or the Philox draw's `order_small_dev`), and `nmf_cd_crit_kernel` tests `nmf_cd_stop_f32`; one
  read per 8 sweeps (NMF_CD_LOOP_CHUNK) instead of 1-2 per sweep. `DKit.cd_rows` (the read-home form) is deleted.
- Label propagation dense graph (`x_neighbors/iter_device.mojo` `op_lp_iterate`): one body `_LpDenseStep` (stopping sum,
  `loop_criterion_below` against the float32 ceiling of tol, the gated dense / raw product or the ELL SpMM op
  `lp_ell_spmm_enqueue`, the gated clamp), one read per LPK_BATCH. Deleted: the default path's stopping-sum read every
  iteration, the `-D MOJOLEARN_C33_FROZEN_CHUNKS` dense-only second copy, `_c33_stop` and `_c43_graph_product`. Same bits
  (the stop decision is the float64 compare's, the ELL product is the dense product's bits).
- Label propagation kNN graph: `lp_iterate_knn` is the only path on every vendor and tier; `lp_fast_resident` returns 1.
  Deleted: `-D MOJOLEARN_LP_FAST_RESIDENT_OFF` (FAST + Apple default since A/B n2-lp-res-taxi, label-propagation taxi
  6,793 -> 2,086 ms, accuracy .7016 same) and `-D MOJOLEARN_IDN_LP_RESIDENT_OFF` (IDENTICAL default since lane
  fam2-neighbors 2026-10-04, same bits), both refused in `core/experiment_guards_cluster.mojo`; and the binding's
  compact-graph loop in `bindings/neighbors_semi_native.mojo` (absdiff_sum read, lp_knn_product and a clamp per
  iteration, n x C allocated per iteration) with `_lp_fast_resident`.

Bits: MDS and NMF stop tests (and MDS's non-metric scale) are float32 cells (`x_decomp/cells.mojo`) on every column, the
host twins (`x_decomp/mds.mojo`, `x_decomp/nmf.mojo`) changed with the device; they were Python's float64 tail. Outputs
change only where the stop iteration moves (a borderline ratio) or for a zero disparity sum. Label propagation: no bit
change.

Restore: `git apply -3 experiments/removed/N4_MDS_LABELPROP_NMF_HOST_LOOPS.patch` (the reverse of the lane on the code
files; the guard entry in `core/experiment_guards_cluster.mojo` is left out). Code recoverable at `f59d913b0b`.
Run owed: MDS, NMF, LabelPropagation / LabelSpreading speed on NVIDIA and AMD (board and paper_compare rows) against
`f59d913b0b`, and the identity lanes mds, nmf, label-propagation, label-spreading at the release.

## Dictionary learning loops as device programs (2026-11-09)

Lane n10-dictl-arima-loops (plan section 4, row "Dictionary learning"). `x_decomp/dictl_dev.mojo`'s two loops read
3 + 2 nc words home per iteration: the used-atom count (`count_gt` of A's diagonal), A[j, j] per atom (`cols` with a
drain and `word`), the resample's draw and std (`resample_atom_dev`), the two cost words (`cost_dev`), and per
MiniBatch step the dictionary change; every row solve (`DKit._code_rows`) also drained. Now each loop enqueues
`DL_CHECK_EVERY` = 4 iterations (state in a ring of slots, cost words in a device array) and reads once; the host
replays the float64 error, forgetting average and stop tests over the chunk in order and takes the stopping slot. The
atom test, the Philox draw, the row pick, the noise and the code column's zeroing are `x_decomp/dictl_resample.mojo`
(the FAST fused update, `x_decomp/dict_fast.mojo`, runs the same kernel between its two launches, so it no longer needs
the used-atom count). Deleted: `resample_atom_dev`, `cost_dev`, the per-atom reads, `_code_rows`'s drain. Bits: none on
an update without an unused atom (same cells, same order; the row std is the same per-row folds computed for every row
at once). A resampled atom's noise scale is now one float32 product `mul(0.01f, std or 1)` on the device and in the host
column (`x_decomp/dictl.mojo::resample_atom`), where it was the float64 product rounded to float32; that changes the bits
of a resampled atom only, on every vendor and the host column together (identity lanes: dictionary-learning,
minibatch-dictionary-learning, sparse-coder when an atom goes unused). Recoverable at f59d913b0b; patch
`experiments/removed/DICTL_HOST_READS.patch` (all code hunks).

  witness word); the stop is a criterion kernel (`sgd_flags_crit_kernel`, `sgd_live_crit_kernel`); the one-vs-rest
  activity, epoch counts and result words are device values (`sgd_mb_ovr_act_kernel`, `sgd_mb_ovr_res_kernel`). Reads:
  once per `sgd_loop_check_every` epochs (no tolerance: once at the bound; with one: Program.fit's
  `fit_epochs_per_read` over the epoch's launches). Deleted: the three host epoch loops, the per-epoch `ctx.synchronize()`
  and stop-word copies, the one-vs-rest host activity lists and `dact` re-uploads, and the per-epoch PA row-norm launch
  (`sgd_rowsq_kernel` once a fit, `_sgd_rowsq_once`). Same kernels, order and operands: no bit change.

  step `_LpKnnStep` on `bounded_device_loop` (the check kernels are the criteria); their hand chunk loops, flag words and
  step counters are deleted (steps taken = the loop's stop iteration - 1). No bit change.
- `x_neighbors_lp_fast_resident` (always 1) deleted with `lp_fast_resident` (device and host), both provider bindings,
  both binding registrations, `x_neighbors/gen.py`, the `_surface_neighbors.py` manifest row, `_lp_fast_resident` and its
  test use.

  the EM loop, so the lifetime drains in `gmm_e_step` / `gmm_m_step` run only without a keep.

Code recoverable at `5b5490960d`. A/B define: `-D MOJOLEARN_SGD_LOOP_CHECK_EVERY=<k>` (1 = the old per-epoch read).

## SmallByteLanguageModelTrainer on the executor (2026-11-09)

Lane x7-byte-lm-on-executor, plan `docs/plans/EXECUTOR_CONSOLIDATION_AND_CLEANUP.md` row X7. Every step, gradient, update and
evaluation of `SmallByteLanguageModelTrainer` (and of ParallelByteLM's shard trainers) runs on ONE captured program per trainer
(`training/byte_lm_program.mojo`): `OPS_EMBEDDING`, one `OPS_ATTN_STEP` per decoder layer (the layer's nine weights packed in one
step-op weights tensor, its keys/values as declared state), `OPS_TRANSPOSE` + `OPS_MATMUL` for the head and the mean
`OPS_CROSS_ENTROPY`. `train_step` / `train_steps` are ONE `Program.fit` (`train_program_control`) over the call's batches; a
recorded attention step is a zero-state prefill with its stages kept, recorded as one custom tape node whose VJP is the transformer
stage rule (`autograd/rules_step_ops.mojo` `StepOpRules`, tag 108). The trainer's flat buffers stay the committed state (export,
logits, rollback); a call's result is copied in after the shadow point and re-scanned.

What was deleted:

- `training/byte_lm.mojo`: the per-layer hand forward `_byte_forward_loss` and `_byte_layer_forward_deferred` (eight
  `llama_decoder_layer_forward` sites), `_byte_backward_tape`, the `IDN_TRAIN_ONE_WAIT` step (`_byte_step_one_wait`), the Apple
  FAST no-sync step (`_afn_byte_step_nosync`), the step-glue update arms (`_byte_glue_update`, `_byte_live_status_launch` /
  `_finish`), the eager-scratch release helpers, the per-layer training stage lists, and the trainer's certified optimizer step
  (`identical_optimizer_step` is no longer called by the trainer; `byte_glue_update_launch` stays for the pooled trainers).
- `autograd/rules_lm.mojo` (`byte_backward_autograd`, `LmRules`, `byte_lm_tape_eligible`), `training/checks/lm_tape_backward_check.mojo`
  and its digests, the `check-lm-tape-backward` pixi task and the `autograd-lm-tape` smoke entry.
- `byte_owner_steps` and operation 12 on the device (`training/byte_lm_native_dispatch.mojo`) and host
  (`training/byte_lm_host_trainer_dispatch.mojo`) columns, and the binding's `while k < n_steps` driver
  (`bindings/byte_lm_trainer_native.mojo` `_run_steps`): operation 1 takes the step count (`p[14]`), opens the session when it is
  not open and exports a 'full' result's gradient, so `train_steps` is one native call. The stateless route keeps one whole-state
  call per batch by design.

Behaviour: a refused `train_steps` call (non-finite loss, a state failing the after-scans) now commits none of its steps on the
device column (it committed the steps before the failed one); the host column still commits step by step and the binding
reconciles either from the session status.

## Integration w6: GPU units one at a time (2026-11-09)

Integration branch `integ/pre-0867-w3` (wave 6, compile-fix lane integ-w6, orchestrator decision).

- `MOJOLEARN_MSEL_UNITS_SERIAL` (lane p3, `lane/p3-msel-parallel-and-process-pool@9d7f5a2af9`, `bindings/msel_cv.mojo`
  `msel_unit_workers`): the old form behind a switch, every CV unit on the calling thread, kept until an NVIDIA / AMD A/B
  of units on vs off. On the Mac the parallel units crashed in Metal command-buffer completion (`cross_val_score`,
  `CalibratedClassifierCV` with `n_jobs` >= 2 or None): the member fits share the process-wide device context
  (`core/neural_context.mojo`) and the owners' caches are not thread-safe. The run-time rule
  `native_unit_device_workers` (`bindings/native_unit_threads.mojo`) now runs units whose member fits run on a GPU (context
  vendor metal, cuda or hip) one at a time and keeps the parallel units on a CPU-only install or the host column. That is
  this switch's form on every GPU, and the CPU is never timed, so the switch decided nothing: retired. The parallel-GPU arm
  stays compiled behind `-D MOJOLEARN_MSEL_UNITS_GPU_PARALLEL` (default off; awaits a thread-safety lane, then the A/B).
  Verdict: retired (redundant), not measured. Bits: none (same fits, same order of results).
- Never reached main: no patch; code recoverable at the lane sha above. The define is refused by
  `core/experiment_guards_trees.mojo`.

## Lane p1-python-callbacks-worst: Python callbacks removed from native operations (2026-11-09)

Branch `lane/p1-python-callbacks-worst` (base `origin/integ/pre-0867-w3` @ `e68654a757`). Not experiments: Python code
that ran inside a native product operation (AGENTS.md "No Python in the runtime"), from the audits
`~/mojolearn-evidence/py-audit-a-imports.md` (worst 1-5, 9, 10, 35, 36 and the Python-side drivers) and
`~/mojolearn-evidence/py-audit-b-callpaths.md` (worst 2-3). Each became native or a refusal before the hook runs.

- `P1_RESAMPLE_OBJECT_GETITEM` (`providers/python/resample_rows_pyapi.mojo`): object and structured-object rows are
  copied as bytes with CPython reference counts at each object leaf (offsets read once from the dtype); StringDType
  rows by one `ndarray.take`. Bits: none (the same references).
- `P1_KMEANS_CALLABLE_INIT` (`bindings/kmeans_native.mojo`): a callable `init` is refused before it is called, naming
  explicit centers, 'k-means++' and 'random' (as MiniBatchKMeans already did). Interface change: callable init refused.
- `P1_SPECTRAL_TOCOO` (`bindings/cfb_spectral.mojo`): exact SciPy COO/CSR/CSC read from stored buffers; other SciPy
  formats densified natively (`host_sparse_dense`); duck-typed sparse objects take the dense admission.
- `P1_NEIGHBORS_GRAPH_TOCSR` (`bindings/neighbors_graph_native.mojo`, new `core/sparse_coo_csr_impl.mojo`): a CSC or COO
  adjacency is grouped by row with a stable parallel counting sort; duplicates kept (SciPy's COO `tocsr()` summed
  them: bits may change for PageRank on a COO input with duplicate entries); BSR/DIA/DOK/LIL refused by name.
- `P1_SEMI_SEED_RANDOMSTATE` (`bindings/neighbors_semi_native.mojo`): the seed word is drawn natively through NumPy's
  BitGenerator capsule (`pcs_seed`), the same word as `randint(0, 2**31, size=1)[0]`. Bits: none.
- `P1_ONEHOT_WARN_IN_NATIVE` (`bindings/prep_encode_native.mojo`): the unknown-category warning goes through the native
  warning path (`bindings/classical_warnings.mojo` `classical_warning`: filters read natively, only the standard
  display hooks admitted, a custom `showwarning` refused; an "error" filter raises `UserWarning`), attributed to the
  caller's frame; the encode context now carries `connect_warnings()`.
- `P1_NATIVE_SKLEARN_TAGS`: tags are built by `_mode.sklearn_tags` (owner exception 2026-10-24); no native code
  imports `sklearn.utils._tags`.
- `P1_DEAD_PY_CURVE_DRIVERS`: Python top-level defs no Python file (product, tests, tools, bench) and no Mojo string
  lookup reaches (AST reachability, docstrings and comments ignored), 91 defs in `_expansion_metrics`,
  `_expansion_decomp`, `_expansion_prep`, `preprocessing`, `linear_model`, `_linalg_impl`, `_expansion_neighbors`,
  `_labels`; lists in `~/mojolearn-evidence/p1/removed_*.tsv`.
- Code recoverable at `e68654a757`; patches `experiments/removed/P1_*.patch` (the reverse of the lane's change to the
  code files).

## Array protocol, labels and list inputs without Python frames (2026-11-09)

Lane `p2-labels-lists-arrays` (P2 of the pre-0.8.67 Python audit follow-up: audit A worst item 6, audit B worst items 4,
5, 7, 8 and 10 and its NATIVE* class), branch `lane/p2-labels-lists-arrays` from `integ/pre-0867-w3` `e68654a757`. Not
experiment defines: Python frames and per-element CPython object loops on product paths. No A/B define: every
replacement computes the same values in the same order (see the bit notes below).

- **Array** (`python/mojolearn/_array.py`, `bindings/array_native.mojo`): the protocol methods and the `flags` /
  `__array_interface__` properties are C `property` objects over `functools.partial(array_native_call, op, context)`, so
  `len(a)`, `a[i]`, `a == b`, `repr(a)`, iteration, `memoryview(a)` and NumPy's interface read enter no Python frame. The
  entry accepts the bound layout `(op, context, array, *args)` beside `(op, array, context, *args)`. Pickle: `__reduce__`
  returns `(copyreg.__newobj__, (cls,), state)` and the native `__setstate__` rebuilds the store; `_restore_array` (a
  Python reconstructor per Array field of every pickled estimator) is gone. A read-only Array restored from a pickle
  keeps its own dtype (the old reconstructor took the view's, so a read-only float16 came back `<u2`).
- **Fallback list**: `array-length-metadata`, the one entry of `python/mojolearn/_runtime_fallbacks.py`, is removed; the
  evidence checker (`tools/release_public_runtime_evidence.py`) refuses any approved fallback, and the profile allows none.
- **Labels** (`python/mojolearn/_labels.py`, `bindings/labels_native_entry.mojo`): `flatten_labels`, `sorted_classes` and
  `decode_labels` are one native call each (ops FLATTEN 5, SORTED 6, DECODE 3). The native ORDER RULE admits exact label
  types only (a subclass's comparison or hash hooks never run), so some refusals are worded as the native walk words
  them. `ClassLabels` pickles through `object.__reduce_ex__`'s C path (`__slotnames__` preset).
- **Per-element loops**: `labels_decode_labels` fills str / bool / object labels in C (`p3_decode_list`);
  `MultiOutputClassifier.predict` object labels by `p3_interleave_columns` / `p3_rows_of`; the classical NB / LDA / QDA
  `score` reads accuracy from the predicted codes (`classical_score_from_codes`); `_object_codes` by `p3_dict_codes`;
  list inputs of the classical admission, `Sequential` and `Program.fit` / `run` / `ImportedProgram.run` read borrowed
  from the C storage (Program inputs: one typed flatten into an output sized once); UMAP categorical list y and GBDT
  int / str `group_id` lists are coded from C storage.
- **Restore**: `git apply experiments/removed/P2_LABELS_LISTS_ARRAYS.patch` (the whole lane reversed, code files only;
  tests and tools keep their new form). Recoverable at `e68654a757`.
- **Guard / records**: no `-D` define was removed, so no guard refusal and no `grid_controls` entry moves.

## Decided B arms: lane fb12-loser-arms (2026-11-17)

Five A/B switches decided with the B arm losing or giving no gain on the NVIDIA L40S (pc-ba08dac006f5-nvidia final2 (`~/mojolearn-evidence/measure-candidate/pc-ba08dac006f5-nvidia/final2/owed-nvidia.json`), NVIDIA L40S, one run per arm, A and B sets of ba08dac006; recorded in
docs/apple-fast/EXPERIMENTS.md by lane fb8-owed-arms; NVIDIA only under AGENTS.md part 8). Each B arm was deleted on
2026-11-15 by an expdel2 lane and restored the same day by lane/expdel2-restore-owed as an owed arm (see the Restored
table); this is the deletion after the measurement. Defaults unchanged, no bit change on any column. Recoverable at
`2203db7094` (the lane's base, preinteg/wave2-20261113). Restore order for the byte LM pair: PROGRAM_STEP first (it
brings back training/byte_lm_program.mojo), then GENERIC_OPS.

## Env arms and unmeasured defines: lane fx-env-dead (2026-11-18)

### MOJOLEARN_XQ_ABS_BALANCE (fx-env-dead)

- What it was: Run-time env read `MOJOLEARN_XQ_ABS_BALANCE=1` (per fit) switched the ADMM residual balancing from the relative rule (prim/eps_p against dual/eps_d, OSQP) to the absolute rule (prim against dual), through request word fp[4] and the `rel` flag of `_balance` / `rel_bal` of `q_tail` on both columns.
- Verdict: DECIDED by quality, recorded in the kernel docstring: the absolute rule compares two norms in different units; on standardized Istella-S and taxi it doubled rho to ~4000x its start, float32 ADMM drifted off the LP optimum (Istella-S r2 -1.7e11) and never met the tolerance (5000 iterations). Speed is never bought with quality. The default (relative) path is unchanged on every column: no bit changes. fp[4] stays in the request layout, unread.
